name: mwiii
title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III (2023)
status: phase 1 draft (2026-10-05): container, dump, primitives located by hand; no tables yet
note: Addresses from the decrypted cod23-cod.exe (PE timestamp 1788250263, the same as the install's), flattened (file offset == RVA). Primitives read by disassembly. The SP zones (sp23) go with sp23-cod.exe, an older build (timestamp 1751952877, 249 asset types, other header sizes): not this profile.
rva_note: file_read = ReadXFile(dst, n). Load_Stream(flag, dst, n) 0x3bbcc80: flag 0 returns at once (the usual meaning, not IW8's inverted one); block 11 memsets, any other reads; then the position advances. A second copy 0x3bbcc30 tests flag == 1 (one caller, 0x314c89f). Load_XAsset 0x3b220a0 calls Load_Stream through a function object (0xc0b3cb8 -> 0xc0b3cc0, set by 0x3bbc930), then tail-calls the type switch 0x3b22100 (Load_<T>Ptr(0, &header, asset)). load_string / load_string_ptr: the text one byte at a time through file_read; load_string_ptr then interns it (AllocateUniqueString 0x3d41bd0). push(block) / pop keep a 16-byte stack at 0xf57c9d0; pop rewinds block 1 and aligns block 2 to 32. insert_ptr: push(15), align 8, 8 bytes, pop. advance(mask): the aligner every reader calls (6 450 callers). alloc 0x3ad90b0(alignment): advance(alignment - 1), returns the stream position (weapon's 0x3b1d183).

asset_dispatch.note: ParseFastFile 0x3bbcb00: file_read of the 0x20-byte XAssetList; push(15); Load_ScriptStringList 0x3b035b0(0, list); pop; push(15); the array aligned (advance 7) and read (count x 16, inline); per asset Load_XAsset(0, &list[i]); pop. The switch is a cmp chain on the type: 239 of 252 types.

stream.machinery_note: the stream init's block table copy (0x3bbc460) and the function object assignment (0x3ad91b0) DB_InitLoadStreams 0x3bbc930 calls: engine code by the reach rule, run for the state they set; the Load_Stream functor class (vtable 0xc283440: invoke, copy, move, destroy), what the function object calls; 0x3ad9070, Load_Stream's function object called by value (weapon's 0x3b1cedf: the reach rule cannot see through its indirect call)
stream.null_page_note: engine lookups the dump leaves empty return null and the loader reads through it (MWIII AllocateUniqueString 0x3d41bd0 skipped; BO7 Load_CustomScriptString 0x3ad7730 falls back to address 8 when the script string map has no entry): a zero page reads as an empty result
stream.stream_objects_note: the Load_Stream function object (vtable slot 0xc0b3cb8, functor 0xc0b3cc0) DB_InitLoadStreams sets: the readers' own read for flag 1
stream.growing_note: reads land in 15 (the main block: 434 MB of the 637 zones recorded up to 10 MB), 1 (temp: pop 0x3bbc710 rewinds it), 3, 6, 10 and 13 (pushed by the level's readers); 11 memsets
stream.loop_rsp_note: rsp stays known past a loop that calls but leaves it unchanged: the stream object's flag is passed by reference in a stack slot after such loops (attachment 0x3b1799c)
stream.not_value_note: a flag bit tested clear through not (0x3b0f8e5: shr eax, 6; not al; test al, 1): the transcriber writes ~x as (2^bits - 1) - x
stream.vex_note: VEX-encoded SSE read as its SSE form (vmovsd in gfx_map_trzone's 0x3aebe90)

asset_link.note: LinkGenericXAsset; asset type info: 48-byte records at 0x90b07f0 (header size u32 at 0, has-name byte at 0x29), names at 0x90b36d0 (GetXAssetTypeName 0x3bb0dc0): 252 types

install_note: Steam install, plain files (no CASC). Games/MWIII/Container.cpp decodes the .ff and applies the .fp beside it. Working set: 596 non-_tr zones and 165 _tr ones of cod23.

stream_init_call.note: DB_InitLoadStreams(zone): the 16 blocks {base, size} from the zone memory's 0x788 into the stream globals (0x3bbc460), and Load_Stream (0x3bbcc80) installed in the function object 0xc0b3cb8 Load_XAsset calls for flag 1

hand_roots_note: the f<rva> readers the hand tables name are transcribed too: the union switch 0x3b04fa0 (scriptable events) whose cases the reach rule does not follow
transcriber_budget_note: a reader whose symbolic run passes 200 000 instructions is refused (the table generation once took over 10 minutes on a handful of them)
